notes.claim: Dividing one number by a fraction asks how many times that fraction fits into the number.
3 divided by a quarter can be read as how many quarters there are in 3, which is 12: a small piece gives a big count.
The reciprocal of a fraction swaps numerator and denominator; a number times its reciprocal is 1, and the reciprocal says how many times the fraction fits into 1.
How many of a fraction are in one is one divided by that fraction, so dividing any number by that fraction is that number times the reciprocal.
To divide fractions, multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second, which is easier than dividing by a fraction directly.
